text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 3.8% today to $423.92, capping a brutal two-week decline of 11%. The main driver is a sharp reversal in oil-market sentiment: yesterday's geopolitical risk premium evaporated when peace negotiations between the U.S. and Iran gained traction, easing fears of supply disruptions that had been pushing crude prices higher. Oil prices dropped Thursday as a result, which hurts refining margins—the spread between what Marathon pays for crude and what it makes selling refined products like gasoline and diesel.

The timing matters: Marathon had rallied 6% just two days earlier (October 26) on fears of Iranian conflict that could choke off Middle Eastern oil. Now that threat has receded. While refineries are running at a robust 92.8% capacity and storage levels remain moderate, a softer crude market strips away one of the main props that had supported energy stocks recently.
